draft.title: Recruiting and selecting staff
card: finding people who might do the job. A business advertises the role, often with a job description that lists the duties and the skills needed.
choosing the best person from those who applied. The business sorts the applications and makes a shortlist of people who fit the role.
Shortlisted people are interviewed, so the business can ask about their skills and experience. It then contacts referees, people who know the applicant's work, to check what they said.
The aim is to choose the person whose skills best fit the role, not just the first person to apply. A good choice saves the cost of hiring again.
draft.remember: Recruit to attract applicants, then select the best fit for the role.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat has received 40 applications for a baker's job. What is the business doing when it picks six to interview?
opts: Selecting, by shortlisting applicants who fit the role
Recruiting, by advertising the role to more people
Selecting, by checking what referees say about them
Recruiting, by writing a list of duties for the job
a.why: Choosing a few people from those who applied is selecting. Advertising and writing duties happen earlier, to attract applicants, which is recruiting.

b.q: Priya interviews Jack for a sales job at her shop in Geelong. Jack says he ran a busy market stall for two years. What should Priya do next to check this claim?
opts: Contact his referees to confirm his work history
Offer him the job because he sounded confident
Advertise the job again to attract more people
Write a new job description for the role
b.why: Referees know the applicant's work, so contacting them checks what Jack said. Hiring on confidence alone skips the check, and advertising again is recruiting, which has already been done.
b.clue: Who knows how Jack worked in the past?

a.best: Selecting, by shortlisting applicants who fit the role

b.best: Contact his referees to confirm his work history
